whyMustafa.heading: A Focused Response to the Learning Challenges Families Face
whyMustafa.subheading: Every learner faces different obstacles. Our approach combines individual teaching, appropriate tutor matching, structured follow-up, and flexible scheduling to provide support that fits the student.

items.title: Lessons That Move Too Quickly
items.challenge: Students may struggle when classroom explanations move forward before they fully understand the previous concept.
items.solution: The tutor adjusts the pace, explanation, examples, and practice to match the student's current understanding.

items.title: Learning Gaps That Build Over Time
items.challenge: Missing foundational skills can make new lessons more difficult and gradually reduce confidence.
items.solution: We identify priority gaps and include the necessary foundational skills within a clear and focused learning plan.

items.title: Difficulty Finding the Right Tutor
items.challenge: A tutor may understand the subject well but may not match the student's curriculum, language, or learning style.
items.solution: Tutor selection considers the subject, grade, curriculum, preferred language, and the student's individual learning needs.

items.title: Limited Visibility for Parents
items.challenge: Families may not always know what the student is learning, where progress is occurring, or what still needs attention.
items.solution: Parents receive practical communication and relevant updates about learning priorities, completed work, and recommended next steps.

items.title: Schedules That Are Difficult to Maintain
items.challenge: School, family responsibilities, and time-zone differences can make regular tutoring difficult to organize.
items.solution: Online lessons are arranged around student availability to support a consistent and manageable learning routine.

items.title: Low Confidence and Learning Motivation
items.challenge: Repeated difficulty can make students hesitant to participate, ask questions, or attempt challenging work.
items.solution: One-to-one lessons provide a supportive environment where the student can ask questions, practise, and progress without classroom pressure.

items.question: How do I get started with Mustafa Academy?
items.answer: Contact us through WhatsApp and share the student's grade, subject, curriculum, preferred teaching language, current learning challenges, and available times. Our team will review the information and help arrange the appropriate next step.

items.question: Is the trial lesson free?
items.answer: A free trial lesson may be arranged for eligible new students before beginning a regular package. The purpose is to understand the student's needs, introduce the tutoring experience, and help determine an appropriate tutor and starting point.

items.question: How is the tutor selected?
items.answer: Tutor selection considers the subject, grade level, curriculum, preferred teaching language, student availability, and individual learning needs. The goal is to provide a suitable match rather than assigning the same tutor profile to every student.

items.question: How long is each lesson?
items.answer: Lesson duration can vary according to the student's age, subject, program, and selected arrangement. The exact lesson duration is confirmed with the family before regular lessons or package payment begins.

items.question: Are lesson times flexible?
items.answer: Yes. Lessons are arranged online according to tutor availability, student availability, school commitments, and time-zone differences. Regular attendance is encouraged to support consistent progress.

items.question: Which subjects and curricula are available?
items.answer: Mustafa Academy supports a range of subjects including Mathematics, English, Science, Physics, Chemistry, French, Arabic, and other available programs. Support may include Canadian, American, Quebec, and other curricula depending on the grade, subject, and available tutor.

items.question: Can we request a different tutor?
items.answer: Families may contact the support team when the current match does not meet the student's academic or communication needs. The situation will be reviewed and an alternative tutor may be considered based on availability.

items.question: How is the student's progress followed?
items.answer: Progress may be followed through lesson feedback, completed work, priority skills, homework follow-up when applicable, and communication with the family. The level of reporting depends on the student's program and tutoring arrangement.

items.question: What happens if a lesson needs to be rescheduled or cancelled?
items.answer: Families should contact the team as early as possible when a lesson cannot be attended. Rescheduling, cancellation, late-notice, and missed-lesson conditions are confirmed before payment and are handled according to the applicable policy.

items.question: How are package payments handled?
items.answer: Package prices are shown in Canadian dollars. Before payment, the family should confirm the number and duration of lessons, payment method, applicable taxes, renewal arrangements, and the relevant cancellation or refund conditions.
